judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain party-identification and effective-date clause; the only definite terms are the names and the 'date it is last signed', neither of which bears more than one reading. It does introduce the plural defined term 'Consultants', but the preamble itself is unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Section 2.a, which pays 'Consultant' in the singular, so the preamble's plural definition sits slightly awkwardly, but the mismatch is a defect of 2.a rather than of the preamble. Nothing else in the short instrument contradicts the parties or effective date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recitals contain soft, unmeasurable language — 'future consulting services to enhance the value for the sale of the property' and services provided 'upon the Company's request' — whose boundary cannot be applied, though recitals are not themselves operative. The Jasper Port/appraisal recital is factual background rather than a promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is the classic 2.3 posture: the recital conditions future services on the Company's request and frames consideration as consulting work, while operative Sections 2.a and 2.b pay a flat 20% on any sale and on the donation tax savings without regard to whether any services were requested or performed. A party resisting payment would naturally argue the recital limits the operative payment obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Profit' is defined as 'total proceeds from a sale, less reasonable expenses, holding costs and expenses relating to transactions regarding the property (i.e. donations, etc)' — 'reasonable expenses' is vague, the definition conspicuously omits the acquisition cost/basis, and 'i.e. donations, etc' is a mechanical misuse of 'i.e.' for 'e.g.' followed by an open-ended 'etc' whose reach is undefined. This is exactly the general catch-all against a one-item list that leaves the deduction category unbounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Section 2.a, which is wholly dependent on this definition, and Section 2.b, which treats the same donation as a source of tax savings to be shared rather than as an expense to be deducted — the two treatments of 'donations' are hard to harmonise. The definition also cannot be applied coherently to a 'sale of a portion' under 2.a without allocating holding costs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Company shall pay Consultant twenty-percent (20%)' uses the singular where the preamble defines two 'Consultants', leaving open whether 20% is the aggregate share or 20% each; 'Upon sale of a portion or all of Delta Bluffs' also gives no mechanism for computing Profit on a partial sale.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The clause is entirely parasitic on the Section 1 definition of 'Profit', which omits acquisition cost and uses an open 'etc' — so the payment obligation inherits that indeterminacy, and it must also be reconciled with Section 2.b's separate donation-based entitlement. The mismatch with the preamble's plural 'Consultants' is a real, if small, internal inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is a comma splice joining a permissive statement ('may realize certain tax savings') to a mandatory one ('Consultants shall be entitled'), so it is unclear whether entitlement is conditioned on savings actually being realised and by whom; 'Company or its principal' extends the trigger to a person who is not a party, and 'once the risk of a federal or state tax audit has expired, which is expected to occur in October 2016' leaves the timing condition and the meaning of 'such savings' genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Section 1, which treats donations as an expense deducted in computing Profit, and against the preamble, which binds only the Company and not 'its principal' — reading 2.b to reach the principal's personal tax savings is difficult to square with either. The recital also describes the donation as already-completed assistance, which cuts against a forward-looking payment condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional merger clause, though it is limited to agreements 'in connection with Delta Bluffs' rather than being unqualified, and it terminates in a comma mid-thought, suggesting the sentence is truncated. Neither feature obviously changes its meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the recitals: an integration clause is the standard vehicle for excluding the extrinsic understandings about consulting services and the Jasper Port appraisal, so it can be pressed into service in the recital-versus-operative fight, but it does not contradict any operative term. The document contains no other clause it conflicts with.
